title: Shapes, Patterns & Data
description: Class 2 IMO — Lines and shapes, sides and corners, growing and repeating patterns, and reading simple pictographs for the Maths Olympiad.

topics.title: Lines and Shapes
topics.concept: A line can be straight or curved. Flat shapes are made of straight lines: a triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners, a square and a rectangle have 4 sides and 4 corners, and a circle is a curved shape with no corners. Solid shapes like a cube, cuboid, sphere, cone and cylinder take up space.

examples.problem: How many corners does a rectangle have?
Which shape is made of one curved line?

recap: Triangle: 3 sides; square/rectangle: 4 sides; circle: no corners.

quiz.q: How many sides does a triangle have?

quiz.explanation: A sphere (ball) rolls because it is round.

topics.title: Patterns
topics.concept: A pattern repeats by a rule. In a repeating pattern, the same set comes again and again (▲■▲■…). In a growing pattern, numbers go up by the same step (2, 4, 6, 8…). Find the rule, then give the next item.

examples.solution: ▲ — the pattern is circle, triangle repeating.

recap: Repeating pattern: the same set comes again.
Growing pattern: numbers go up by a fixed step.

quiz.explanation: After two squares comes a triangle.

topics.title: Reading Pictographs
topics.concept: A pictograph shows data using pictures, where each picture stands for a number of things. To read it, count the pictures in each row and find how many that means. We can then say which has the most or least, and find totals or differences.

examples.problem: If 1 ★ = 1 book and a child has 4 ★, how many books?
Class A has 5 ★ and Class B has 3 ★ (1 ★ = 1 child). Which has more?

recap: Each picture stands for a number of things.
Count pictures to compare most/least and find totals.

quiz.q: If 1 ⚽ = 2 goals, then 3 ⚽ means how many goals?
Apples: 6 pictures; Oranges: 4 pictures (1 picture = 1 fruit). How many more apples?

questions.q: Which shape is the odd one out:  triangle, square, rectangle, circle?
questions.explanation: A circle has no corners; the others all have corners.

questions.q: Continue:  A, C, E, ___ (skip one letter each time)?
questions.explanation: Skipping one letter: A, C, E, G.

questions.q: How many corners does a square have?
A brick is shaped like a ___ ?
How many sides does a rectangle have?
In the growing pattern 10, 20, 30, 40, the rule is 'add ___'.
questions.explanation: Each number is 10 more than the one before.

questions.q: On a pictograph 1 🌳 = 5 trees. A park row shows 4 🌳. How many trees?
Fruits sold: Mango 7 pictures, Apple 5, Banana 3 (1 picture = 1 fruit). Which sold the most?
A pictograph shows Class 2A read 8 books and Class 2B read 5 books. How many books in all?
Continue the pattern:  1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ___ (the step grows by 1 each time)?
A pictograph uses 1 ⭐ = 10 stickers. Riya has 3 ⭐ and Sara has 5 ⭐. How many more stickers does Sara have?
